reasoning_traces.think:
The system operates under a dual-tiered credit model: free tier (500 credits/month) and paid tier. The core consumption driver is the settlement cron which consumes 168 credits/day when a paid key is active. In-season sports expansion increases consumption to 2,016 credits/day (7 sports × 3 markets × 1 region × 3 credits). Using Poisson arrival processes, we derive depletion time T = Q/C. For 500 credits and 2,016/day, T ≈ 0.25 days. This triggers a soft failure mode where the system must either scale down cadence or switch to paid tier. The 14-hour threshold in commit `cd4e77d6` reflects conservative bounds before skipping final sport in refresh cycle. Dualities emerge between cost control and data freshness, with failure modes including quota exhaustion and 429 errors. The system's robustness depends on adaptive scheduling and failover mechanisms.
